items.title: No monthly catheter-days series for the 12 wards
items.whyItMatters: Quarterly point counts cannot show change from noise.
items.opportunity: Build 12 months of flowsheet baseline for Hospitals A to C and start point counts in Hospital D before its start.

items.title: Infection effects cannot be detected on 12 wards
items.whyItMatters: At about 2 infections per 1,000 catheter days, a year of 12 wards gives few events, and published effects are imprecise (claim c2).
items.opportunity: Report infections descriptively and keep catheter days as the primary measure.

items.title: Mixed measurement sources across hospitals
items.whyItMatters: Hospital D cannot produce flowsheet catheter days, and switching sources within a series looks like change (claim c5).
items.opportunity: Use point counts for Hospital D's whole series and analyse it with a site-specific level.

items.title: Nurses lack explicit authority to remove
items.whyItMatters: Uncertainty about removal without an order keeps catheters in.
items.opportunity: Approve a nurse-driven removal protocol through each hospital's medical advisory committee before its start.

items.title: Older men after surgery bear the reinsertion risk
items.whyItMatters: Reinsertion concentrates in older surgical men with retention (claim c6).
items.opportunity: Report reinsertion by age group and service, with a bladder scan before reinsertion.

errorsFound: The need lists infections as a possible primary measure; with these numbers infections can only be described.
reevaluation: The gaps favour a staggered multiple-baseline Lean project with catheter days as the primary measure, infections descriptive, reinsertion as balancing, and a site-specific measure for Hospital D.
summary: Five gaps; the missing series and the undetectable infection effect are high severity.
